question.problem:
A veterinarian collects data on a puppy's height $y$ (in inches) at certain times $x$ (in months) since it was born. The equation of the corresponding linear regression line for this data is 

$$
y=2.2x+3.5.
$$

What is the residual after $5$ months if the actual height of the $5$-month old puppy is $15.5\,in?$
question.worked_solution:
The residual equals the difference between the actual value of the dependent variable and the value estimated using the linear regression model:

$$
\text{Residual}=\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated}
$$

 

First, we compute the estimated height using our linear regression model:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{y} & =2.2x+3.5 \\  & =2.2(5)+3.5 \\  & =14.5\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Residual} & =\text{Actual}-\text{Estimated} \\  & =y-\overset{^}{y} \\  & =15.5-14.5 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residual is $1\,in.$
